role: Format D held open. The theory gets its hook and its exhibits, the official explanation and the cloud-seeding concession are both spoken, and the film stops on the one observation that keeps the argument going rather than resolving it.
editorial_note: Every line is either attributed to the theory or true. The official explanation is still in the film at L03 — water vapour freezing into ice, not CO2, which is an invisible gas and could not make a visible line — and L04 concedes up front that aircraft really do disperse material, that cloud seeding is an ordinary licensed industry and that US operators report every operation. What this cut deliberately does NOT do is resolve L06. Two aircraft in the same sky genuinely do behave differently, and the reason is that a contrail only persists in air already cold and wet enough to hold it, in a layer often only a few hundred metres thick — fly a level above or below it and you leave nothing. That explanation was written, voiced and cut; it is preserved in git history and is four lines of script away if the ending is ever wanted closed.
voice_note: Running sentences, hedges left in, no chains of one-word fragments. The first half is told the way somebody repeats a thing they keep seeing; L04 is the flat turn.

lines.en: There's a theory that the lines planes leave behind aren't exhaust, but something sprayed on the cities below.
lines.vo_direction: Level. Reporting what other people believe, not selling it.

lines.en: They've been photographed for thirty years — grids over airports, crosses over capitals.
The official answer is contrails — water vapour from the engines freezing into ice.
Planes do spray things — cloud seeding is real and gets reported to the government.
lines.vo_direction: Plain. This is a concession, not a reveal.

lines.en: But here's what keeps the theory alive.
Two planes cross the same sky, one leaves a trail for hours, the other nothing.
lines.vo_direction: Slow on the last three words.

lines.en: Maybe the truth comes out soon.
lines.vo_direction: Quiet, unhurried. An open door, not a promise.
